title: In Hungary in 1946, prices doubled roughly every 15 hours
body: After the Second World War, Hungary suffered the worst hyperinflation on record. In July 1946 the monthly inflation rate reached about 41.9 quadrillion percent, so prices doubled roughly every 15 hours. The central bank issued a 100 quintillion pengő note, the highest face value of any banknote ever circulated, before replacing the pengő with the forint in August 1946.
